ref: DAR — Revelation ch. 6: The Seven Seals
title: The Seven Seals
voicePrompt: In your own words, explain Smith's central thesis: that the seven seals trace the religious history of the church from the Christian era to Christ's coming. Walk through what each of the first six seals (the four horses, the martyrs, and the signs in the heavens) represents and why he reads the sixth seal as the period we now live in.

questions.stem: According to the chapter, what class of events do the seven seals embrace, and how do they differ from the seven trumpets?
options: The seals denote events of a religious character (the history of the church), while the trumpets denote great political commotions (war) among the nations
The seals denote political wars, while the trumpets denote religious revivals in the church
The seals and the trumpets denote the very same events described twice over
The seals reach only to the time of Constantine, after which the trumpets take over the history
questions.explanation: Smith states the trumpets are a symbol of war and denote political commotions among the nations, while the seals 'denote events of a religious character, and contain the history of the church from the opening of the Christian era to the coming of Christ.' He explicitly rejects the view that the seals stop at Constantine and the trumpets continue from there.

questions.stem: What does the chapter say the white horse of the first seal represents?
options: The corruption that entered the church after Constantine
The triumphs and purity of the gospel in the first century of this dispensation
The persecuting rule of the papacy
The literal armies of the Roman Empire
questions.explanation: The chapter calls the white horse 'a fit emblem of the triumphs of the gospel in the first century of this dispensation,' with the horse's whiteness denoting 'the purity of faith in that age' and the crowned rider going forth conquering signifying the zeal and success of the earliest ministers.

questions.stem: How does the chapter interpret the change in the horses' colors from white to red to black to pale?
options: As the four seasons of the year applied to church festivals
As four different geographic regions where the gospel spread
As a progressive corruption of the church: red signals corruption beginning, black a period of darkness and moral corruption, and the pale horse the papacy's deadly persecuting rule
As four successive Roman emperors who each favored Christianity
questions.explanation: Smith reads the red horse as the original purity beginning to be corrupted, the black horse as 'a period of great darkness and moral corruption in the church,' and the pale (sickly) horse, whose rider is Death, as the papacy's 'unrebuked, unrestrained, and persecuting rule,' commencing about A.D. 538.

questions.stem: Regarding the souls under the altar in the fifth seal, what position does the chapter take?
options: That they prove the conscious, disembodied state of the dead in heaven
That the altar is the altar of incense in heaven where the saints rejoice
That the language is personification (like Abel's blood crying from the ground), so the slain martyrs are not proved to be alive or conscious
That the souls are the angels who minister to the churches
questions.explanation: The chapter argues the 'popular view' of conscious disembodied souls is inadmissible, that the altar is the altar of sacrifice on earth, and that the souls' cry is personification (comparing it to Abel's blood crying from the ground in Genesis 4:10), concluding the martyrs 'were not alive when John saw them' and first live again at the resurrection of the just.

questions.stem: What does the chapter say the white robes given to the martyrs of the fifth seal signify, and when were they given?
options: Literal garments handed out in heaven at the moment of each martyr's death
The vindication of the martyrs' reputation, accomplished as the Reformation exposed the papacy's corruptions and the martyrs' good names were restored
The purity of the apostolic church in the first century
The resurrection bodies the martyrs will receive at the second coming
questions.explanation: The chapter explains the martyrs had gone to the grave defamed by Rome, but as the Reformation exposed the papal abominations, 'the reputation of the church going down, and that of the martyrs coming up,' the martyrs were vindicated and honored — 'White robes were thus given unto every one of them.'

questions.stem: According to the chapter, which historical events fulfilled the first three signs of the sixth seal (earthquake, darkened sun, moon as blood, and falling stars)?
options: The fall of Rome, the rise of Islam, and the Crusades
The Lisbon earthquake of 1755, the dark day of May 19, 1780 (with the night moon appearing as blood), and the meteoric shower of November 13, 1833
The eruption of Vesuvius, an eclipse in A.D. 538, and a comet in 1798
The French Revolution, the American Revolution, and the Reformation
questions.explanation: Smith identifies the great earthquake as the Lisbon earthquake of Nov. 1, 1755, the darkening of the sun as the dark day of May 19, 1780 (whose following night had the moon appear as blood), and the falling stars as the great meteoric shower of Nov. 13, 1833.

questions.stem: The chapter notes a shift in language between the fifth and sixth seals. How does it describe and explain this shift?
options: The language shifts from literal to figurative because the events became more spiritual
There is no shift; all the seals use identical figurative language
The language shifts from highly figurative to strictly literal, possibly because the sixth seal's events occur when prophecy was to be unsealed and understood plainly
The language shifts from Greek to Hebrew to mark a new prophetic period
questions.explanation: The chapter states that between the fifth and sixth seals 'there seems to be a sudden and entire change in the language, from the highly figurative to the strictly literal,' and suggests this occurs because the sixth seal's events transpire at a time when these things were to be fully understood, so they are 'laid before us in plain and unmistakable language.'

questions.stem: Where does the chapter place the present-day reader within the sixth seal's events?
options: After all the signs are complete, waiting only for the seventh seal to open
Standing between verses 13 and 14 — past signs (earthquake, sun, moon, stars) fulfilled, now waiting for the heavens to depart as a scroll
Before the earthquake of the sixth seal has even begun
Within the fifth seal's 'little season' of continued persecution
questions.explanation: On 'And the Heaven Departed as a Scroll,' the chapter says 'We stand between the 13th and 14th verses of this chapter. We wait for the heavens to depart as a scroll' — the past signs are fulfilled and the remaining events (departing heavens, second coming) lie in the future.
